model: Eaton Power Xpert PXM 2000 via BASgatewayLX
applies_to: Eaton Power Xpert PXM 2000 series meters on Modbus, read by a BASgatewayLX.
summary: Gateway profile for the Eaton PXM 2000: 329 objects (254 AI, 11 AO, 48 BI, 16 BO), 95 polled by default. Inputs give voltages, currents, W/VAR/VA and PF per phase and total, frequency, received/delivered/net energy, VAR-hours and per-phase energy, plus unpolled demand, THD and I/O states; unpolled outputs test pulse outputs and relays and reset accumulators.
notes: Built from Contemporary Controls' BASgatewayLX Modbus device profile Eaton_PXM2000_Meter_LX.csv; the profile maps the registers in the maker's Modbus register document (https://www.ccontrols.com/support/dp/EatonPXM2000.PDF).
Object instances are the ones this profile assigns when it is loaded into the gateway. A site that edited or rebuilt the profile may use different instances.
Only 95 of the 329 rows are flagged for polling in the profile; the rest are served only after you tick them in the gateway. Their descriptions say "not polled by default".

The CSV has no read/write column: Analog/Binary Inputs are read-only and Analog/Binary Outputs are commandable (priority array), which is how the gateway maps them (access inferred). Descriptions give the Modbus register each object reads.
Some names appear more than once in the profile as published (VAR-hours Net Phase C; Positive Watts Phase C Average; Angle Phase A Current...); they are kept as printed and told apart by instance.

integration.summary: Map total watts (3-phase), delivered energy (Wh) and received energy (Wh) first. The listed objects are read-only.
setup: The BASgatewayLX presents each Modbus device as its own virtual BACnet device on BACnet IP; give it a unique device instance and Modbus address (serial) or IP address (Modbus TCP) when you add it with this profile.
One BASgatewayLX handles up to 100 Modbus devices and 1000 polled points in total, so leave unneeded rows unpolled.
gotchas: Outputs include firmware reprogramming and meter restart commands; never poll or write them.
Unpolled rows do not appear as BACnet objects until enabled in the gateway's device profile page.
